params.body:
#722 worked and its last step did not, which only showed once it ran for real.

Tag `v2026.09.21` was created and the release "Stocklist Dealer v2026.09.21" was published, in sixteen seconds. The badge in the README stayed at v2.0.0, and `release-badge.yml` had not run at all.

The cause is a documented GitHub behaviour I should have carried into the design: **an event created with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not start other workflows.** That exists to stop runaway chains, and it quietly broke the last link — the release is published, and the workflow waiting for a published release never hears it.

So the badge is written by `release.yml` itself, right after publishing, instead of by a second workflow that has to be woken. `release-badge.yml` stays for a release published by hand, and now says so in its own header.

One thing worth noting: that push makes the loop guard load-bearing. Until now the `if` that skips a badge commit was belt-and-braces, because with `GITHUB_TOKEN` no cascade could happen anyway. Now it is the thing that stops release.yml from handing itself another version every time it writes a badge. The test pins it.

R P1-1.23 says where the badge is written and why it is not the other workflow.
params.title: The badge follows the release
